newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president signs new constitution into law.
newsitem.headline: Polish president signs new constitution into law.

text.p: President Aleksander Kwasniewski signed Poland's new constitution on Wednesday, clearing the last hurdle before the controversial charter becomes law in three months' time.
"Today, the Polish nation receives a solid foundation and its citizens strong guarantees of freedom and personal rights," the formerly communist president said during the televised ceremony.
"I signed the constitition of a free and democratic Poland, a constitituion which confirms respect for the nation and for its roots."
The Supreme Court ruled on Tuesday that a May referendum which approved the constitution was valid, overruling protests that a low turnout invalidated the vote.
The constitution, replacing a Stalin-era document and interim arrangements made since the 1989 fall of communism, is a compromise between government and opposition parties now in parliament.
It has been strongly criticised by the Catholic Church and its right-leaning political allies, now underrepresented in parliament but hoping to win elections on September 21.

Supporters say the constitution is Western in style and embraces people of all faiths or none, but critics argue that it fails to underline a close association between Poland's majority Christian faith and its national identity.

The church also opposes it because it does not include a clause effectively banning abortion, which is now legal in Poland but could be severely restricted under a separate court ruling earlier this year.

The pro-church Solidarity trade union and allied parties campaigned against the constitution in the referendum, which approved it by 53 to 46 percent of the vote. Only 42.9 percent of the electorate took part.
The Solidarity Election Action has promised to try to amend the constitution if it defeats the dominant ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance party in the Septemeber election.
